questions.question: What is the main idea of this paper, and why is it different from generating objects separately?
questions.expected: Single-image compositional 3D reconstruction; conditions each object on neighboring geometry and physical relations for spatial compatibility, including occluded contacts.

questions.question: If a cup is sitting on a table, which one gets reconstructed first, and how does the system decide?
questions.expected: Table first; VLM physical dependency graph, topological ordering, previously generated support geometry conditions cup.

questions.question: What information does the model use so nearby objects do not float or go through each other?
questions.expected: Spatial context: UDF, nearest surface direction and normal; relation type embeddings. These are learned guidance, not a hard guarantee.

questions.question: How does it fill in parts of an object that are hidden behind another object?
questions.expected: Visible-to-invisible cross-attention; invisible tokens query visible tokens as keys/values, at DiT layers in both stages.

questions.question: Was Tetris3D trained on Toys4K or ComOb, and which datasets were used to test it?
questions.expected: Training ComOb; evaluation Toys4K, Picasso, MessyKitchens. Toys4K object sources disjoint from training.

questions.question: What are the five relation labels used for conditioning? Are those exactly the same as the interaction types used to generate ComOb?
questions.expected: Conditioning: stack, lean, contain, touch, none. Dataset construction: stack, lean, contain, pile, touch. Distinguish none from pile.

questions.question: How many scenes and annotated samples does ComOb contain? Are those the same count?
What GPUs were used for training, and how long did each of the two models take to train?
questions.expected: Two NVIDIA H200 GPUs, batch16; sparse structure about7days, structured latent about9days.

questions.question: Which tools provide depth, object masks, and object identification at inference?
questions.expected: MoGe3 depth/camera; SAM3 masks; Qwen3-VL-30B distinct object identification. Do not swap roles.

questions.question: Does the paper guarantee that every reconstructed scene obeys physics? What can still go wrong?
questions.expected: No; learned guidance not hard constraints; depth/segmentation/relation errors can propagate autoregressively.

questions.question: What monthly subscription price and warranty does this paper promise for deploying Tetris3D in Santio?
questions.expected: No reported subscription price or Santio warranty; abstain instead of inventing.

questions.question: In Table 3 on Toys4K, what penetration depth (PD) is reported for the full model versus the model without interaction conditioning? Which is lower?
